claims.original_text: Achieves 72.4 NDS on the nuScenes validation set using camera-only input, outperforming BEVFormer (56.9 NDS) and approaching LiDAR-based CenterPoint (67.3 NDS).
claims.summary: The claim's BEVFormer baseline (56.9 NDS) is confirmed by multiple sources, but there's a significant discrepancy in the CenterPoint comparison - evidence shows CenterPoint achieved 65.5 NDS, not the claimed 67.3 NDS. The startup's claimed 72.4 NDS performance cannot be verified from the available evidence.

evidence_for.text: BEVFormer achieves 56.9% NDS on nuScenes test set for camera-only detection, confirming the baseline comparison
BEVFofmer-C achieves 56.9% NDS in camera-only manner, matching the claimed baseline

evidence_against.text: CenterPoint achieved 65.5 NDS on nuScenes benchmark, not the claimed 67.3 NDS

red_flags: No verification of the claimed 72.4 NDS performance in available evidence
Inaccurate baseline comparison with CenterPoint (claims 67.3 NDS vs evidence showing 65.5 NDS)
follow_up_questions: Can you provide the peer-reviewed paper or official leaderboard submission showing your 72.4 NDS result?
Why does your CenterPoint baseline differ from the published 65.5 NDS result?
Are you comparing results on the same dataset split (validation vs test set) as the baseline methods?

claims.original_text: End-to-end perception pipeline runs in 23ms on a single NVIDIA Orin, achieving 43 FPS — 2.8x faster than Waymo's published camera perception latency of 65ms.
claims.summary: The claim cannot be verified from the provided evidence. While NVIDIA Orin documentation confirms the hardware's deep learning capabilities (38-74% performance contribution from DLA), none of the sources contain the specific 65ms Waymo camera perception latency figure that the startup uses for comparison.

evidence_for.text: NVIDIA Orin hardware is confirmed capable of deep learning workloads with DLA contributing 38-74% to total performance depending on power mode
NVIDIA DRIVE AGX platform is designed to process complex autonomous driving workloads

red_flags: no verification of Waymo's 65ms baseline claim
follow_up_questions: Can you provide the specific Waymo publication or source that documents the 65ms camera perception latency?
What is the exact hardware configuration and power mode of the NVIDIA Orin used in your benchmarks?
Can you share independent benchmark results or allow testing of your perception pipeline on standardized datasets?

claims.original_text: Maintains 94% of clear-weather detection accuracy in heavy rain and fog conditions on our internal benchmark of 180,000 annotated adverse-weather frames.
claims.summary: The claim of maintaining 94% accuracy in adverse weather appears highly optimistic given available evidence. Research shows significant performance degradation in adverse conditions, with one study documenting up to 40% increase in miss rates during fog and night conditions, contradicting the startup's claimed minimal accuracy loss.

evidence_for.text: AWD-YOLO algorithm offers superior solution for object detection under adverse weather conditions
Dual-Teacher Feature Alignment framework proposed for adverse weather detection shows improvements

evidence_against.text: Up to 40% rise in miss rate in night or fog proves that camera-only perception under weather influences is not safe enough
Adverse weather conditions significantly degrade image quality causing texture blurring and reduced contrast

red_flags: Internal benchmark with no public validation
No peer-reviewed publication of their specific results
follow_up_questions: Can you provide the methodology and composition of your 180,000 annotated adverse-weather frame dataset?
What is your baseline clear-weather accuracy that the 94% retention is measured against?
Have these results been validated on any public benchmarks or third-party datasets?

claims.original_text: First camera-only perception stack to be certified for ASIL-D functional safety compliance under ISO 26262, enabling deployment in production L3+ vehicles.
claims.summary: The claim appears partially supported but lacks specificity. Helm.ai has achieved ISO 26262 certification for their camera-only perception stack, but the evidence shows ASIL-B(D) certification rather than full ASIL-D. The 'first' claim cannot be verified from the available evidence.

evidence_for.text: Helm.ai has achieved ISO 26262 ASIL-B(D) certification for their camera-vision-only AV stack using proprietary Deep Teaching technology
Helm.ai has been certified to meet ISO 26262 standards and assessed by UL Solutions for their Level 3 Urban Perception System

evidence_against.text: The evidence shows ASIL-B(D) certification rather than the claimed ASIL-D certification

red_flags: superlative claim - 'first' cannot be verified from available evidence
potential misrepresentation of certification level - evidence shows ASIL-B(D) while claim states ASIL-D
follow_up_questions: Can you provide the actual ISO 26262 certification documents showing ASIL-D compliance rather than ASIL-B(D)?
What evidence supports the claim of being the 'first' camera-only perception stack with this certification?
Which specific components or functions within your system have achieved ASIL-D versus lower ASIL levels?

claims.original_text: Our proprietary depth estimation module produces dense 3D reconstructions from monocular video at 42 FPS.
claims.summary: The claim of 42 FPS dense 3D reconstruction from monocular video is technically feasible based on recent research. SLAM3R demonstrates real-time dense 3D reconstruction from monocular RGB, and OpenVINO optimization shows quantized models can achieve real-time performance for monocular depth estimation.

evidence_for.text: SLAM3R system achieves real-time and high-quality dense 3D reconstruction from monocular RGB
OpenVINO quantized models enable real-time operation for monocular depth estimation with massive performance increases
Real-time dense reconstruction can be achieved with efficient algorithms and modern computational hardware

evidence_against.text: No specific FPS benchmarks found in the search results to validate the claimed 42 FPS performance

red_flags: No specific FPS benchmark data provided to validate the precise 42 FPS claim
No evidence of proprietary technology differentiation from existing open research like SLAM3R
follow_up_questions: What specific hardware configuration achieves 42 FPS and how does this compare to SLAM3R's performance?
What proprietary innovations differentiate your depth estimation from existing real-time monocular systems?
Can you provide benchmark comparisons showing your 42 FPS performance against academic baselines?
